e-491.knowledge_point: Using Integration by Parts to Compute an Indefinite Integral Containing an Exponential Expression
e-491.worked_solution:
To solve this integral, we use the by-parts formula, given by

$$
\int uv' \, \textrm{d}x= uv - \int vu' \, \textrm{d}x.
$$

We need to express $\displaystyle  \int xe^{7x} \textrm{d}x$ as $\displaystyle  \int uv'\,\textrm{d}x.$ Therefore, we set

$$
\begin{aligned}u=x\, & ⟹\,{u}^{′}=1 \\ {v}^{′}={e}^{7x}\, & ⟹\,v=\frac{1}{7}{e}^{7x}.\end{aligned}
$$

We substitute the above into the integration by parts formula, and we get the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}\int u{v}^{′}\,\text{d}x & =uv-\int v{u}^{′}\,\text{d}x \\ \int x\cdot {e}^{7x}\,\text{d}x & =x\cdot \frac{1}{7}{e}^{7x}-\int \frac{1}{7}{e}^{7x}\cdot 1\,\text{d}x\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we calculate the integral:

$$
\begin{aligned}\int x{e}^{7x}\,\text{d}x & =\frac{1}{7}x{e}^{7x}-\frac{1}{7}\int {e}^{7x}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{1}{7}x{e}^{7x}-\frac{1}{7}(\frac{{e}^{7x}}{7})+C \\  & =\frac{1}{7}x{e}^{7x}-\frac{1}{49}{e}^{7x}+C\end{aligned}
$$

e-492.knowledge_point: Using Integration by Parts to Compute an Indefinite Integral Containing a Trigonometric Expression
e-492.worked_solution:
To solve this integral, we use the by-parts formula, given by

$$
\int uv'\,\textrm{d}x= uv- \int vu'\,\textrm{d}x.
$$

We need to express $\displaystyle \int x \cos{2x} \textrm{d}x$ as $\displaystyle \int uv'\,\textrm{d}x.$ Therefore, we set

$$
\begin{aligned}u=x\, & ⟹\,{u}^{′}=1 \\ {v}^{′}=\operatorname{cos}⁡2x\, & ⟹\,v=\frac{1}{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡2x.\end{aligned}
$$

We substitute the above into the integration by parts formula, and we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\int u{v}^{′}\,\text{d}x & =uv-\int v{u}^{′}\,\text{d}x \\ \int x\operatorname{cos}⁡2x\,\text{d}x & =x\cdot \frac{1}{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡2x-\int \frac{1}{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡2x\cdot 1\,\text{d}x.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we calculate the integral, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\int x\operatorname{cos}⁡2x\,\text{d}x & =\frac{1}{2}x\operatorname{sin}⁡2x-\frac{1}{2}\int \operatorname{sin}⁡2x\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{1}{2}x\operatorname{sin}⁡2x-\frac{1}{2}(-\frac{1}{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡2x)+C \\  & =\frac{1}{2}x\operatorname{sin}⁡2x+\frac{1}{4}\operatorname{cos}⁡2x+C\end{aligned}
$$

e-6209.knowledge_point: Computing a Definite Integral Using Integration by Parts
e-6209.worked_solution:
Let's use integration by parts. We set

$$
\begin{aligned}u=x\, & ⟹\,{u}^{′}=1 \\ {v}^{′}=\operatorname{sin}⁡(5x) & ⟹\,v=-\frac{1}{5}\operatorname{cos}⁡(5x).\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting the above into the integration by parts formula, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\int u{v}^{′}\,\text{d}x & =uv-\int v{u}^{′}\,\text{d}x \\ \int x\cdot \operatorname{sin}⁡(5x)\,\text{d}x & =-x\cdot \frac{1}{5}\operatorname{cos}⁡(5x)-\int (-\frac{1}{5}\operatorname{cos}⁡(5x))\cdot 1\,\text{d}x.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we evaluate the integral and get

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{\pi /5}x\operatorname{sin}⁡(5x)\,\text{d}x & =-{\frac{1}{5}x\operatorname{cos}⁡(5x)|}_{0}^{\pi /5}+\frac{1}{5}{\int }_{0}^{\pi /5}\operatorname{cos}⁡(5x)\,\text{d}x \\  & =-{\frac{1}{5}x\operatorname{cos}⁡(5x)|}_{0}^{\pi /5}+{\frac{1}{5}(\frac{\operatorname{sin}⁡(5x)}{5})|}_{0}^{\pi /5} \\  & =[-\frac{1}{5}\cdot \frac{\pi }{5}\operatorname{cos}⁡(\pi )+\frac{1}{5}\cdot 0\cdot \operatorname{cos}⁡(0)]+[\frac{1}{25}\operatorname{sin}⁡(\pi )-\frac{1}{25}\operatorname{sin}⁡(0)] \\  & =[-\frac{\pi }{25}\cdot (-1)+0]+[0-0] \\  & =\frac{\pi }{25}.\end{aligned}
$$

decision.explanation: Using integration by parts with u=3x-4 and v=-e^{-3x}/3 gives -(3x-4)e^{-3x}/3-e^{-3x}/3+C=(1-x)e^{-3x}+C. Its derivative is (3x-4)e^{-3x}.

after.name: Question 1
after.worked_solution:
To solve this integral, we use the by-parts formula, given by

$$
\int u{v}^{′}\,\text{d}x=uv-\int v{u}^{′}\,\text{d}x.
$$

We need to express $\int (3x-4){e}^{-3x}\text{d}x$ as $\int u{v}^{′}\,\text{d}x.$ Therefore, we set

$$
\begin{aligned}u=3x-4\, & ⟹\,{u}^{′}=3 \\ {v}^{′}={e}^{-3x}\, & ⟹\,v=-\frac{{e}^{-3x}}{3}.\end{aligned}
$$

We substitute the above into the integration by parts formula, and we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\int u{v}^{′}\,\text{d}x & =uv-\int v{u}^{′}\,\text{d}x \\ \int (3x-4)\cdot {e}^{-3x}\,\text{d}x & =(3x-4)\cdot (-\frac{{e}^{-3x}}{3})-\int (-\frac{{e}^{-3x}}{3})\cdot 3\,\text{d}x.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we calculate the integral, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\int (3x-4){e}^{-3x}\,\text{d}x & =-\frac{(3x-4){e}^{-3x}}{3}+\int {e}^{-3x}\,\text{d}x \\  & =-\frac{(3x-4){e}^{-3x}}{3}-\frac{{e}^{-3x}}{3}+C \\  & =-\frac{(3x-3){e}^{-3x}}{3}+C \\  & =(1-x){e}^{-3x}+C\end{aligned}
$$

Question 1
?

Calculate ∫(3x−4)e−3xdx.

a
(2x−1)e−3x3+C
b
(2x−1)e−3x+C
c
(1−x)e−3x+C
d
(2−3x)e−3x+C
e
(2−x)e−3x3+C
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

To solve this integral, we use the by-parts formula, given by

∫uv′dx=uv−∫vu′dx.

We need to express ∫(3x−4)e−3xdx as ∫uv′dx. Therefore, we set

u=3x−4⟹u′=3v′=e−3x⟹v=−e−3x3.

We substitute the above into the integration by parts formula, and we get

∫uv′dx=uv−∫vu′dx∫(3x−4)⋅e−3xdx=(3x−4)⋅(−e−3x3)−∫(−e−3x3)⋅3dx.

Finally, we calculate the integral, as follows:

∫(3x−4)e−3xdx=−(3x−4)e−3x3+∫e−3xdx=−(3x−4)e−3x3−e−3x3+C=−(3x−3)e−3x3+C=(1−x)e−3x+C

content.knowledge_point: Using Integration by Parts to Compute an Indefinite Integral Containing an Exponential Expression
content.worked_solution:
To solve this integral, we use the by-parts formula, given by

$$
\int u{v}^{′}\,\text{d}x=uv-\int v{u}^{′}\,\text{d}x.
$$

We need to express $\int (3x-4){e}^{-3x}\text{d}x$ as $\int u{v}^{′}\,\text{d}x.$ Therefore, we set

$$
\begin{aligned}u=3x-4\, & ⟹\,{u}^{′}=3 \\ {v}^{′}={e}^{-3x}\, & ⟹\,v=-\frac{{e}^{-3x}}{3}.\end{aligned}
$$

We substitute the above into the integration by parts formula, and we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\int u{v}^{′}\,\text{d}x & =uv-\int v{u}^{′}\,\text{d}x \\ \int (3x-4)\cdot {e}^{-3x}\,\text{d}x & =(3x-4)\cdot (-\frac{{e}^{-3x}}{3})-\int (-\frac{{e}^{-3x}}{3})\cdot 3\,\text{d}x.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we calculate the integral, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\int (3x-4){e}^{-3x}\,\text{d}x & =-\frac{(3x-4){e}^{-3x}}{3}+\int {e}^{-3x}\,\text{d}x \\  & =-\frac{(3x-4){e}^{-3x}}{3}-\frac{{e}^{-3x}}{3}+C \\  & =-\frac{(3x-3){e}^{-3x}}{3}+C \\  & =(1-x){e}^{-3x}+C\end{aligned}
$$

Question 2

∫4xe8xdx=

a
 xe8x2−e8x4+C
b
xe8x4+5e8x16+C
c
 xe8x8−e8x16+C
d
 xe8x2−e8x16+C
e

decision.explanation: Integration by parts with u=4x and dv=e^{8x}dx gives xe^{8x}/2−(1/2)∫e^{8x}dx=xe^{8x}/2−e^{8x}/16+C.

after.name: Question 2
after.worked_solution:
To solve this integral, we use the by-parts formula, given by

$$
\int u{v}^{′}\,\text{d}x=uv-\int v{u}^{′}\,\text{d}x.
$$

We need to express $\int 4x{e}^{8x}\text{d}x$ as $\int u{v}^{′}\,\text{d}x.$ Therefore, we set

$$
\begin{aligned}u=4x\, & ⟹\,{u}^{′}=4 \\ {v}^{′}={e}^{8x}\, & ⟹\,v=\frac{1}{8}{e}^{8x}.\end{aligned}
$$

We substitute the above into the integration by parts formula, and we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\int u{v}^{′}\,\text{d}x & =uv-\int v{u}^{′}\,\text{d}x \\ \int 4x\cdot {e}^{8x}\,\text{d}x & =4x\cdot \frac{1}{8}{e}^{8x}-\int \frac{1}{8}{e}^{8x}\cdot 4\,\text{d}x.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we calculate the integral, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\int 4x{e}^{8x}\,\text{d}x & =\frac{1}{2}x{e}^{8x}-\frac{1}{2}\int {e}^{8x}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{x{e}^{8x}}{2}-\frac{{e}^{8x}}{16}+C\end{aligned}
$$

∫4xe8xdx=

a
 xe8x2−e8x4+C
b
xe8x4+5e8x16+C
c
 xe8x8−e8x16+C
d
 xe8x2−e8x16+C
e
 3xe8x8+e8x12+C
Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

To solve this integral, we use the by-parts formula, given by

∫uv′dx=uv−∫vu′dx.

We need to express ∫4xe8xdx as ∫uv′dx. Therefore, we set

u=4x⟹u′=4v′=e8x⟹v=18e8x.

We substitute the above into the integration by parts formula, and we get

∫uv′dx=uv−∫vu′dx∫4x⋅e8xdx=4x⋅18e8x−∫18e8x⋅4dx.

Finally, we calculate the integral, as follows:

∫4xe8xdx=12xe8x−12∫e8xdx=xe8x2−e8x16+C

verification.explanation: The revealed solution confirms option d. Integration by parts gives xe^{8x}/2−e^{8x}/16+C, whose derivative is 4xe^{8x}.

content.knowledge_point: Using Integration by Parts to Compute an Indefinite Integral Containing an Exponential Expression
content.worked_solution:
To solve this integral, we use the by-parts formula, given by

$$
\int u{v}^{′}\,\text{d}x=uv-\int v{u}^{′}\,\text{d}x.
$$

We need to express $\int 4x{e}^{8x}\text{d}x$ as $\int u{v}^{′}\,\text{d}x.$ Therefore, we set

$$
\begin{aligned}u=4x\, & ⟹\,{u}^{′}=4 \\ {v}^{′}={e}^{8x}\, & ⟹\,v=\frac{1}{8}{e}^{8x}.\end{aligned}
$$

We substitute the above into the integration by parts formula, and we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\int u{v}^{′}\,\text{d}x & =uv-\int v{u}^{′}\,\text{d}x \\ \int 4x\cdot {e}^{8x}\,\text{d}x & =4x\cdot \frac{1}{8}{e}^{8x}-\int \frac{1}{8}{e}^{8x}\cdot 4\,\text{d}x.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we calculate the integral, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\int 4x{e}^{8x}\,\text{d}x & =\frac{1}{2}x{e}^{8x}-\frac{1}{2}\int {e}^{8x}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{x{e}^{8x}}{2}-\frac{{e}^{8x}}{16}+C\end{aligned}
$$

Question 3

∫x5xdx=

a
5xln⁡5(x+1ln⁡5)+C
b
5xln⁡5(x−1)+C
c
5xln⁡5(x−1ln⁡5)+C

decision.explanation: Integration by parts with u=x and dv=5^x dx gives x5^x/ln(5)−5^x/(ln(5))^2+C. Factoring yields option c.

after.name: Question 3
after.worked_solution:
To solve this integral, we use the by-parts formula, given by

$$
\int u{v}^{′}\,\text{d}x=uv-\int v{u}^{′}\,\text{d}x.
$$

We need to express $\int x{5}^{x}\text{d}x$ as $\int u{v}^{′}\,\text{d}x.$ Therefore, we set

$$
\begin{aligned}u=x\, & ⟹\,{u}^{′}=1 \\ {v}^{′}={5}^{x}\, & ⟹\,v=\frac{{5}^{x}}{\operatorname{ln}⁡(5)}.\end{aligned}
$$

We substitute the above into the integration by parts formula, and we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\int u{v}^{′}\,\text{d}x & =uv-\int v{u}^{′}\,\text{d}x \\ \int x\cdot {5}^{x}\,\text{d}x & =x\cdot \frac{{5}^{x}}{\operatorname{ln}⁡(5)}-\int \frac{{5}^{x}}{\operatorname{ln}⁡(5)}\cdot 1\,\text{d}x.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we calculate the integral, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\int x{5}^{x}\,\text{d}x & =\frac{x{5}^{x}}{\operatorname{ln}⁡(5)}-\int \frac{{5}^{x}}{\operatorname{ln}⁡(5)}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{x{5}^{x}}{\operatorname{ln}⁡(5)}-\frac{{5}^{x}}{(\operatorname{ln}⁡(5))^{2}}+C \\  & =\frac{{5}^{x}}{\operatorname{ln}⁡5}(x-\frac{1}{\operatorname{ln}⁡5})+C\end{aligned}
$$

∫x5xdx=

a
5xln⁡5(x+1ln⁡5)+C
b
5xln⁡5(x−1)+C
c

e
5xln⁡5(1−xln⁡5)+C
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

To solve this integral, we use the by-parts formula, given by ∫uv′dx=uv−∫vu′dx.

We need to express ∫x5xdx as ∫uv′dx. Therefore, we set

u=x⟹u′=1v′=5x⟹v=5xln⁡(5).

We substitute the above into the integration by parts formula, and we get

∫uv′dx=uv−∫vu′dx∫x⋅5xdx=x⋅5xln⁡(5)−∫5xln⁡(5)⋅1dx.

Finally, we calculate the integral, as follows:

∫x5xdx=x5xln⁡(5)−∫5xln⁡(5)dx=x5xln⁡(5)−5x(ln⁡(5))2+C=5xln⁡5(x−1ln⁡5)+C

content.knowledge_point: Using Integration by Parts to Compute an Indefinite Integral Containing an Exponential Expression
content.worked_solution:
To solve this integral, we use the by-parts formula, given by

$$
\int u{v}^{′}\,\text{d}x=uv-\int v{u}^{′}\,\text{d}x.
$$

We need to express $\int x{5}^{x}\text{d}x$ as $\int u{v}^{′}\,\text{d}x.$ Therefore, we set

$$
\begin{aligned}u=x\, & ⟹\,{u}^{′}=1 \\ {v}^{′}={5}^{x}\, & ⟹\,v=\frac{{5}^{x}}{\operatorname{ln}⁡(5)}.\end{aligned}
$$

We substitute the above into the integration by parts formula, and we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\int u{v}^{′}\,\text{d}x & =uv-\int v{u}^{′}\,\text{d}x \\ \int x\cdot {5}^{x}\,\text{d}x & =x\cdot \frac{{5}^{x}}{\operatorname{ln}⁡(5)}-\int \frac{{5}^{x}}{\operatorname{ln}⁡(5)}\cdot 1\,\text{d}x.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we calculate the integral, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\int x{5}^{x}\,\text{d}x & =\frac{x{5}^{x}}{\operatorname{ln}⁡(5)}-\int \frac{{5}^{x}}{\operatorname{ln}⁡(5)}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{x{5}^{x}}{\operatorname{ln}⁡(5)}-\frac{{5}^{x}}{(\operatorname{ln}⁡(5))^{2}}+C \\  & =\frac{{5}^{x}}{\operatorname{ln}⁡5}(x-\frac{1}{\operatorname{ln}⁡5})+C\end{aligned}
$$

Question 4
?

Calculate the integral ∫(x+7)e2x+5dx.

a
−xe2x+54+e2x+52+C
b
−(x+7)e2x+54+e2x+52+C
c
xe2x+54−e2x+54+C
d
(x+7)e2x+52−e2x+54+C
e
(x+7)e2x+54−xe2x+54+C
Submit

decision.explanation: Integration by parts with u=x+7 and dv=e^{2x+5}dx gives (x+7)e^{2x+5}/2−(1/2)∫e^{2x+5}dx=(x+7)e^{2x+5}/2−e^{2x+5}/4+C.

after.name: Question 4
after.worked_solution:
To solve this integral, we use the by-parts formula, given by

$$
\int u{v}^{′}\,\text{d}x=uv-\int v{u}^{′}\,\text{d}x.
$$

We need to express $\int (x+7){e}^{2x+5}\,\text{d}x$ as $\int u{v}^{′}\,\text{d}x.$ Therefore, we set

$$
\begin{aligned}u=x+7\, & ⟹\,{u}^{′}=1 \\ {v}^{′}={e}^{2x+5}\, & ⟹\,v=\frac{{e}^{2x+5}}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

We substitute the above into the integration by parts formula, and we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\int u{v}^{′}\,\text{d}x & =uv-\int v{u}^{′}\,\text{d}x \\ \int (x+7)\cdot {e}^{2x+5}\,\text{d}x & =(x+7)\cdot \frac{{e}^{2x+5}}{2}-\int \frac{{e}^{2x+5}}{2}\cdot 1\,\text{d}x.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we calculate the integral, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\int (x+7){e}^{2x+5}\,\text{d}x & =\frac{(x+7){e}^{2x+5}}{2}-\frac{1}{2}\int {e}^{2x+5}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{(x+7){e}^{2x+5}}{2}-\frac{{e}^{2x+5}}{4}+C\end{aligned}
$$

Question 4
?

Calculate the integral ∫(x+7)e2x+5dx.

a
−xe2x+54+e2x+52+C
b
−(x+7)e2x+54+e2x+52+C
c
xe2x+54−e2x+54+C
d
(x+7)e2x+52−e2x+54+C
e
(x+7)e2x+54−xe2x+54+C
Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

To solve this integral, we use the by-parts formula, given by

∫uv′dx=uv−∫vu′dx.

We need to express ∫(x+7)e2x+5dx as ∫uv′dx. Therefore, we set

u=x+7⟹u′=1v′=e2x+5⟹v=e2x+52.

We substitute the above into the integration by parts formula, and we get

∫uv′dx=uv−∫vu′dx∫(x+7)⋅e2x+5dx=(x+7)⋅e2x+52−∫e2x+52⋅1dx.

Finally, we calculate the integral, as follows:

∫(x+7)e2x+5dx=(x+7)e2x+52−12∫e2x+5dx=(x+7)e2x+52−e2x+54+C

content.knowledge_point: Using Integration by Parts to Compute an Indefinite Integral Containing an Exponential Expression
content.worked_solution:
To solve this integral, we use the by-parts formula, given by

$$
\int u{v}^{′}\,\text{d}x=uv-\int v{u}^{′}\,\text{d}x.
$$

We need to express $\int (x+7){e}^{2x+5}\,\text{d}x$ as $\int u{v}^{′}\,\text{d}x.$ Therefore, we set

$$
\begin{aligned}u=x+7\, & ⟹\,{u}^{′}=1 \\ {v}^{′}={e}^{2x+5}\, & ⟹\,v=\frac{{e}^{2x+5}}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

We substitute the above into the integration by parts formula, and we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\int u{v}^{′}\,\text{d}x & =uv-\int v{u}^{′}\,\text{d}x \\ \int (x+7)\cdot {e}^{2x+5}\,\text{d}x & =(x+7)\cdot \frac{{e}^{2x+5}}{2}-\int \frac{{e}^{2x+5}}{2}\cdot 1\,\text{d}x.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we calculate the integral, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\int (x+7){e}^{2x+5}\,\text{d}x & =\frac{(x+7){e}^{2x+5}}{2}-\frac{1}{2}\int {e}^{2x+5}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{(x+7){e}^{2x+5}}{2}-\frac{{e}^{2x+5}}{4}+C\end{aligned}
$$

decision.explanation: Integration by parts with u=6x and dv=e^{-3x}dx gives −2xe^{-3x}+2∫e^{-3x}dx=−2xe^{-3x}−2e^{-3x}/3+C, matching option a.

after.name: Question 5
after.worked_solution:
To solve this integral, we use the by-parts formula, given by

$$
\int u{v}^{′}\,\text{d}x=uv-\int v{u}^{′}\,\text{d}x.
$$

We need to express $\int 6x{e}^{-3x}\text{d}x$ as $\int u{v}^{′}\,\text{d}x.$ Therefore, we set

$$
\begin{aligned}u=6x\, & ⟹\,{u}^{′}=6 \\ {v}^{′}={e}^{-3x}\, & ⟹\,v=-\frac{{e}^{-3x}}{3}.\end{aligned}
$$

We, substitute the above into the integration by parts formula, and we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\int u{v}^{′}\,\text{d}x & =uv-\int v{u}^{′}\,\text{d}x \\ \int 6x\cdot {e}^{-3x}\,\text{d}x & =6x\cdot (-\frac{{e}^{-3x}}{3})-\int (-\frac{{e}^{-3x}}{3})\cdot 6\,\text{d}x \\  & =-2x{e}^{-3x}+2\int {e}^{-3x}\,\text{d}x.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we calculate the integral, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\int 6x{e}^{-3x}\,\text{d}x & =-2x{e}^{-3x}+2\int {e}^{-3x}\,\text{d}x \\  & =-2x{e}^{-3x}-\frac{2{e}^{-3x}}{3}+C\end{aligned}
$$

after.worked_solution:
To solve this integral, we use the by-parts formula, given by

$$
\int u{v}^{′}\,\text{d}x=uv-\int v{u}^{′}\,\text{d}x.
$$

We need to express $\int 6x\operatorname{cos}⁡(x)\text{d}x$ as $\int u{v}^{′}\,\text{d}x.$ Therefore, we set

$$
\begin{aligned}u=6x\, & ⟹\,{u}^{′}=6 \\ {v}^{′}=\operatorname{cos}⁡(x)\, & ⟹\,v=\operatorname{sin}⁡(x).\end{aligned}
$$

We substitute the above into the integration by parts formula, and we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\int u{v}^{′}\,\text{d}x & =uv-\int v{u}^{′}\,\text{d}x \\ \int 6x\cdot \operatorname{cos}⁡(x)\,\text{d}x & =6x\cdot \operatorname{sin}⁡(x)-\int \operatorname{sin}⁡(x)\cdot 6\,\text{d}x.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we calculate the integral, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\int 6x\operatorname{cos}⁡(x)\,\text{d}x & =6x\operatorname{sin}⁡(x)-6\int \operatorname{sin}⁡(x)\,\text{d}x \\  & =6x\operatorname{sin}⁡(x)-6(-\operatorname{cos}⁡(x))+C \\  & =6x\operatorname{sin}⁡(x)+6\operatorname{cos}⁡(x)+C\end{aligned}
$$

Question 6
?

∫6xcos⁡(x)dx=

a
xcos⁡6x−xsin⁡6x+C
b
xcos⁡6x+xsin⁡6x+C
c
6xsin⁡x+6cos⁡x+C
d
−6xsin⁡x+6cos⁡x+C
e
−6xcos⁡x−cos⁡x+C
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

To solve this integral, we use the by-parts formula, given by

∫uv′dx=uv−∫vu′dx.

We need to express ∫6xcos⁡(x)dx as ∫uv′dx. Therefore, we set

u=6x⟹u′=6v′=cos⁡(x)⟹v=sin⁡(x).

We substitute the above into the integration by parts formula, and we get

∫uv′dx=uv−∫vu′dx∫6x⋅cos⁡(x)dx=6x⋅sin⁡(x)−∫sin⁡(x)⋅6dx.

Finally, we calculate the integral, as follows:

∫6xcos⁡(x)dx=6xsin⁡(x)−6∫sin⁡(x)dx=6xsin⁡(x)−6(−cos⁡(x))+C=6xsin⁡(x)+6cos⁡(x)+C

content.knowledge_point: Using Integration by Parts to Compute an Indefinite Integral Containing a Trigonometric Expression
content.worked_solution:
To solve this integral, we use the by-parts formula, given by

$$
\int u{v}^{′}\,\text{d}x=uv-\int v{u}^{′}\,\text{d}x.
$$

We need to express $\int 6x\operatorname{cos}⁡(x)\text{d}x$ as $\int u{v}^{′}\,\text{d}x.$ Therefore, we set

$$
\begin{aligned}u=6x\, & ⟹\,{u}^{′}=6 \\ {v}^{′}=\operatorname{cos}⁡(x)\, & ⟹\,v=\operatorname{sin}⁡(x).\end{aligned}
$$

We substitute the above into the integration by parts formula, and we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\int u{v}^{′}\,\text{d}x & =uv-\int v{u}^{′}\,\text{d}x \\ \int 6x\cdot \operatorname{cos}⁡(x)\,\text{d}x & =6x\cdot \operatorname{sin}⁡(x)-\int \operatorname{sin}⁡(x)\cdot 6\,\text{d}x.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we calculate the integral, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\int 6x\operatorname{cos}⁡(x)\,\text{d}x & =6x\operatorname{sin}⁡(x)-6\int \operatorname{sin}⁡(x)\,\text{d}x \\  & =6x\operatorname{sin}⁡(x)-6(-\operatorname{cos}⁡(x))+C \\  & =6x\operatorname{sin}⁡(x)+6\operatorname{cos}⁡(x)+C\end{aligned}
$$

after.name: Question 7
after.worked_solution:
To solve this integral, we use the by-parts formula, given by

$$
\int u{v}^{′}\,\text{d}x=uv-\int v{u}^{′}\,\text{d}x.
$$

We need to express $\int 10x\operatorname{cos}⁡(x)\text{d}x$ as $\int u{v}^{′}\,\text{d}x.$ Therefore, we set

$$
\begin{aligned}u=10x\, & ⟹\,{u}^{′}=10 \\ {v}^{′}=\operatorname{cos}⁡(x)\, & ⟹\,v=\operatorname{sin}⁡(x).\end{aligned}
$$

We substitute the above into the integration by parts formula, and we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\int u{v}^{′}\,\text{d}x & =uv-\int v{u}^{′}\,\text{d}x \\ \int 10x\cdot \operatorname{cos}⁡(x)\,\text{d}x & =10x\cdot (\operatorname{sin}⁡(x))-\int (\operatorname{sin}⁡(x))\cdot 10\,\text{d}x.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we calculate the integral, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\int 10x\operatorname{cos}⁡(x)\,\text{d}x & =10x\operatorname{sin}⁡(x)-10\int \operatorname{sin}⁡(x)\,\text{d}x \\  & =10x\operatorname{sin}⁡(x)+10\operatorname{cos}⁡(x)+C\end{aligned}
$$

$$
\begin{aligned}\int u{v}^{′}\,\text{d}x & =uv-\int v{u}^{′}\,\text{d}x \\ \int 10x\cdot \operatorname{cos}⁡(x)\,\text{d}x & =10x\cdot (\operatorname{sin}⁡(x))-\int (\operatorname{sin}⁡(x))\cdot 10\,\text{d}x.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we calculate the integral, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\int 10x\operatorname{cos}⁡(x)\,\text{d}x & =10x\operatorname{sin}⁡(x)-10\int \operatorname{sin}⁡(x)\,\text{d}x \\  & =10x\operatorname{sin}⁡(x)+10\operatorname{cos}⁡(x)+C\end{aligned}
$$

after.name: Question 8
after.worked_solution:
To solve this integral, we use the by-parts formula, given by

$$
\int u{v}^{′}\,\text{d}x=uv-\int v{u}^{′}\,\text{d}x.
$$

We need to express $\int 3x\operatorname{cos}⁡(3x)\text{d}x$ as $\int u{v}^{′}\,\text{d}x.$ Therefore, we set

$$
\begin{aligned}u=3x\, & ⟹\,{u}^{′}=3 \\ {v}^{′}=\operatorname{cos}⁡(3x)\, & ⟹\,v=\frac{\operatorname{sin}⁡(3x)}{3}.\end{aligned}
$$

We substitute the above into the integration by parts formula, and we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\int u{v}^{′}\,\text{d}x & =uv-\int v{u}^{′}\,\text{d}x \\ \int 3x\cdot \operatorname{cos}⁡(3x)\,\text{d}x & =3x\cdot (\frac{\operatorname{sin}⁡(3x)}{3})-\int (\frac{\operatorname{sin}⁡(3x)}{3})\cdot 3\,\text{d}x.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we calculate the integral, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\int 3x\operatorname{cos}⁡(3x)\,\text{d}x & =x\operatorname{sin}⁡(3x)-\int \operatorname{sin}⁡(3x)\,\text{d}x \\  & =x\operatorname{sin}⁡(3x)+\frac{\operatorname{cos}⁡(3x)}{3}+C\end{aligned}
$$

Question 8
?

∫3xcos⁡(3x)dx=

a
 sin⁡(3x)−xcos⁡(3x)3+C
b
 3sin⁡(3x)+xcos⁡(3x)6+C
c
 xsin⁡(3x)+cos⁡(3x)3+C
d
 2xsin⁡(3x)+cos⁡(3x)3+C
e
 xsin⁡(3x)3−cos⁡(3x)9+C
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

To solve this integral, we use the by-parts formula, given by

∫uv′dx=uv−∫vu′dx.

We need to express ∫3xcos⁡(3x)dx as ∫uv′dx. Therefore, we set

u=3x⟹u′=3v′=cos⁡(3x)⟹v=sin⁡(3x)3.

We substitute the above into the integration by parts formula, and we get

∫uv′dx=uv−∫vu′dx∫3x⋅cos⁡(3x)dx=3x⋅(sin⁡(3x)3)−∫(sin⁡(3x)3)⋅3dx.

Finally, we calculate the integral, as follows:

∫3xcos⁡(3x)dx=xsin⁡(3x)−∫sin⁡(3x)dx=xsin⁡(3x)+cos⁡(3x)3+C

content.knowledge_point: Using Integration by Parts to Compute an Indefinite Integral Containing a Trigonometric Expression
content.worked_solution:
To solve this integral, we use the by-parts formula, given by

$$
\int u{v}^{′}\,\text{d}x=uv-\int v{u}^{′}\,\text{d}x.
$$

We need to express $\int 3x\operatorname{cos}⁡(3x)\text{d}x$ as $\int u{v}^{′}\,\text{d}x.$ Therefore, we set

$$
\begin{aligned}u=3x\, & ⟹\,{u}^{′}=3 \\ {v}^{′}=\operatorname{cos}⁡(3x)\, & ⟹\,v=\frac{\operatorname{sin}⁡(3x)}{3}.\end{aligned}
$$

We substitute the above into the integration by parts formula, and we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\int u{v}^{′}\,\text{d}x & =uv-\int v{u}^{′}\,\text{d}x \\ \int 3x\cdot \operatorname{cos}⁡(3x)\,\text{d}x & =3x\cdot (\frac{\operatorname{sin}⁡(3x)}{3})-\int (\frac{\operatorname{sin}⁡(3x)}{3})\cdot 3\,\text{d}x.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we calculate the integral, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\int 3x\operatorname{cos}⁡(3x)\,\text{d}x & =x\operatorname{sin}⁡(3x)-\int \operatorname{sin}⁡(3x)\,\text{d}x \\  & =x\operatorname{sin}⁡(3x)+\frac{\operatorname{cos}⁡(3x)}{3}+C\end{aligned}
$$

Question 9
?

Calculate ∫xcsc2⁡xdx.

a
 −2xcot⁡x−ln⁡|sin⁡x|+C
b
 −xcot⁡x−2ln⁡|cos⁡x|+C
c
 xtan⁡x−ln⁡|cos⁡x|+C
d
 xtan⁡x−2ln⁡|sin⁡x|+C
e
 −xcot⁡x+ln⁡|sin⁡x|+C
Submit

decision.explanation: Integration by parts with u=x and dv=csc²(x)dx gives −x cot(x)+∫cot(x)dx=−x cot(x)+ln|sin(x)|+C, matching option e.

after.name: Question 9
after.worked_solution:
To solve this integral, we use the by-parts formula, given by

$$
\int u{v}^{′}\,\text{d}x=uv-\int v{u}^{′}\,\text{d}x.
$$

We need to express $\int x{csc}^{2}⁡x\text{d}x$ as $\int u{v}^{′}\,\text{d}x.$ Therefore we set

$$
\begin{aligned}u=x\, & ⟹\,{u}^{′}=1 \\ {v}^{′}={csc}^{2}⁡x\, & ⟹\,v=-\operatorname{cot}⁡x.\end{aligned}
$$

We substitute the above into the integration by parts formula, and we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\int u{v}^{′}\,\text{d}x & =uv-\int v{u}^{′}\,\text{d}x \\ \int x\cdot {csc}^{2}⁡x\,\text{d}x & =x\cdot (-\operatorname{cot}⁡x)-\int (-\operatorname{cot}⁡x)\cdot 1\,\text{d}x \\  & =-x\operatorname{cot}⁡x+\int \frac{\operatorname{cos}⁡x}{\operatorname{sin}⁡x}\,\text{d}x.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we calculate the integral using the substitution $u=\operatorname{sin}⁡x,$ where $\text{d}u=\operatorname{cos}⁡x\,\text{d}x,$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\int x{csc}^{2}⁡(x)\,\text{d}x & =-x\operatorname{cot}⁡x+\int \frac{\operatorname{cos}⁡x}{\operatorname{sin}⁡x}\,\text{d}x \\  & =-x\operatorname{cot}⁡x+\int \frac{1}{u}\,\text{d}u \\  & =-x\operatorname{cot}⁡x+\operatorname{ln}⁡|u|+C \\  & =-x\operatorname{cot}⁡x+\operatorname{ln}⁡|\operatorname{sin}⁡x|+C\end{aligned}
$$

Question 9
?

Calculate ∫xcsc2⁡xdx.

a
 −2xcot⁡x−ln⁡|sin⁡x|+C
b
 −xcot⁡x−2ln⁡|cos⁡x|+C
c
 xtan⁡x−ln⁡|cos⁡x|+C
d
 xtan⁡x−2ln⁡|sin⁡x|+C
e
 −xcot⁡x+ln⁡|sin⁡x|+C
Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

To solve this integral, we use the by-parts formula, given by

∫uv′dx=uv−∫vu′dx.

We need to express ∫xcsc2⁡xdx as ∫uv′dx. Therefore we set

u=x⟹u′=1v′=csc2⁡x⟹v=−cot⁡x.

We substitute the above into the integration by parts formula, and we get

∫uv′dx=uv−∫vu′dx∫x⋅csc2⁡xdx=x⋅(−cot⁡x)−∫(−cot⁡x)⋅1dx=−xcot⁡x+∫cos⁡xsin⁡xdx.

Finally, we calculate the integral using the substitution u=sin⁡x, where du=cos⁡xdx, as follows:

∫xcsc2⁡(x)dx=−xcot⁡x+∫cos⁡xsin⁡xdx=−xcot⁡x+∫1udu=−xcot⁡x+ln⁡|u|+C=−xcot⁡x+ln⁡|sin⁡x|+C

verification.explanation: The worked solution confirms option e. Differentiating −x cot(x)+ln|sin(x)| gives −cot(x)+x csc²(x)+cot(x)=x csc²(x).

content.knowledge_point: Using Integration by Parts to Compute an Indefinite Integral Containing a Trigonometric Expression
content.worked_solution:
To solve this integral, we use the by-parts formula, given by

$$
\int u{v}^{′}\,\text{d}x=uv-\int v{u}^{′}\,\text{d}x.
$$

We need to express $\int x{csc}^{2}⁡x\text{d}x$ as $\int u{v}^{′}\,\text{d}x.$ Therefore we set

$$
\begin{aligned}u=x\, & ⟹\,{u}^{′}=1 \\ {v}^{′}={csc}^{2}⁡x\, & ⟹\,v=-\operatorname{cot}⁡x.\end{aligned}
$$

We substitute the above into the integration by parts formula, and we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\int u{v}^{′}\,\text{d}x & =uv-\int v{u}^{′}\,\text{d}x \\ \int x\cdot {csc}^{2}⁡x\,\text{d}x & =x\cdot (-\operatorname{cot}⁡x)-\int (-\operatorname{cot}⁡x)\cdot 1\,\text{d}x \\  & =-x\operatorname{cot}⁡x+\int \frac{\operatorname{cos}⁡x}{\operatorname{sin}⁡x}\,\text{d}x.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we calculate the integral using the substitution $u=\operatorname{sin}⁡x,$ where $\text{d}u=\operatorname{cos}⁡x\,\text{d}x,$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\int x{csc}^{2}⁡(x)\,\text{d}x & =-x\operatorname{cot}⁡x+\int \frac{\operatorname{cos}⁡x}{\operatorname{sin}⁡x}\,\text{d}x \\  & =-x\operatorname{cot}⁡x+\int \frac{1}{u}\,\text{d}u \\  & =-x\operatorname{cot}⁡x+\operatorname{ln}⁡|u|+C \\  & =-x\operatorname{cot}⁡x+\operatorname{ln}⁡|\operatorname{sin}⁡x|+C\end{aligned}
$$

after.name: Question 10
after.worked_solution:
To solve this integral, we use the by-parts formula, given by

$$
\int u{v}^{′}\,\text{d}x=uv-\int v{u}^{′}\,\text{d}x.
$$

We need to express $\int (2x+3)\operatorname{sin}⁡(x)\text{d}x$ as $\int u{v}^{′}\,\text{d}x.$ Therefore, we set

$$
\begin{aligned}u=2x+3\, & ⟹\,{u}^{′}=2 \\ {v}^{′}=\operatorname{sin}⁡(x)\, & ⟹\,v=-\operatorname{cos}⁡(x).\end{aligned}
$$

We substitute the above into the integration by parts formula, and we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\int u{v}^{′}\,\text{d}x & =uv-\int v{u}^{′}\,\text{d}x \\ \int (2x+3)\cdot \operatorname{sin}⁡(x)\,\text{d}x & =(2x+3)\cdot (-\operatorname{cos}⁡(x))-\int (-\operatorname{cos}⁡(x))\cdot 2\,\text{d}x.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we calculate the integral, as follows

$$
\begin{aligned}\int (2x+3)\operatorname{sin}⁡(x)\text{d}x & =-(2x+3)\operatorname{cos}⁡(x)+2\int \operatorname{cos}⁡(x)\,\text{d}x \\  & =-(2x+3)\operatorname{cos}⁡(x)+2\operatorname{sin}⁡(x)+C\end{aligned}
$$

content.worked_solution:
To solve this integral, we use the by-parts formula, given by

$$
\int u{v}^{′}\,\text{d}x=uv-\int v{u}^{′}\,\text{d}x.
$$

We need to express $\int (2x+3)\operatorname{sin}⁡(x)\text{d}x$ as $\int u{v}^{′}\,\text{d}x.$ Therefore, we set

$$
\begin{aligned}u=2x+3\, & ⟹\,{u}^{′}=2 \\ {v}^{′}=\operatorname{sin}⁡(x)\, & ⟹\,v=-\operatorname{cos}⁡(x).\end{aligned}
$$

We substitute the above into the integration by parts formula, and we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\int u{v}^{′}\,\text{d}x & =uv-\int v{u}^{′}\,\text{d}x \\ \int (2x+3)\cdot \operatorname{sin}⁡(x)\,\text{d}x & =(2x+3)\cdot (-\operatorname{cos}⁡(x))-\int (-\operatorname{cos}⁡(x))\cdot 2\,\text{d}x.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we calculate the integral, as follows

$$
\begin{aligned}\int (2x+3)\operatorname{sin}⁡(x)\text{d}x & =-(2x+3)\operatorname{cos}⁡(x)+2\int \operatorname{cos}⁡(x)\,\text{d}x \\  & =-(2x+3)\operatorname{cos}⁡(x)+2\operatorname{sin}⁡(x)+C\end{aligned}
$$

decision.explanation: Integration by parts gives F(x)=−(3x/2+3/4)e^{-2x}. Thus F(0)−F(−1)=−3/4−3e²/4=−3(e²+1)/4, matching option a.

after.name: Question 11
after.worked_solution:
Let's use integration by parts. We set

$$
\begin{aligned}u=3x & ⇒ & {u}^{′}=3 \\ {v}^{′}={e}^{-2x} & ⇒ & v=-\frac{{e}^{-2x}}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting the above into the integration by parts formula, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\int u{v}^{′}\,\text{d}x & =uv-\int v{u}^{′}\,\text{d}x \\ \int 3x\cdot {e}^{-2x}\,\text{d}x & =3x\cdot (-\frac{{e}^{-2x}}{2})-\int (-\frac{{e}^{-2x}}{2})\cdot 3\,\text{d}x \\  & =-\frac{3x{e}^{-2x}}{2}+\frac{3}{2}\int {e}^{-2x}\,\text{d}x.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we evaluate the integral and get

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{-1}^{0}3x{e}^{-2x}\,\text{d}x & =-\frac{3x{e}^{-2x}}{2}{|}_{-1}^{0}+\frac{3}{2}{\int }_{-1}^{0}{e}^{-2x}\,\text{d}x \\  & =-\frac{3x{e}^{-2x}}{2}{|}_{-1}^{0}-\frac{3}{4}{e}^{-2x}{|}_{-1}^{0} \\  & =-\frac{3}{2}[0{e}^{-2(0)}-(-1){e}^{-2(-1)}]-\frac{3}{4}[{e}^{-2(0)}-{e}^{-2(-1)}] \\  & =-\frac{3}{2}[0+{e}^{2}]-\frac{3}{4}[1-{e}^{2}] \\  & =-\frac{3}{2}{e}^{2}-\frac{3}{4}+\frac{3}{4}{e}^{2} \\  & =-\frac{3}{4}{e}^{2}-\frac{3}{4} \\  & =-\frac{3}{4}({e}^{2}+1).\end{aligned}
$$

Evaluate ∫−103xe−2xdx.

b

EXPLANATION

Let's use integration by parts. We set

u=3x⇒u′=3v′=e−2x⇒v=−e−2x2. Substituting the above into the integration by parts formula, we get

∫uv′dx=uv−∫vu′dx∫3x⋅e−2xdx=3x⋅(−e−2x2)−∫(−e−2x2)⋅3dx=−3xe−2x2+32∫e−2xdx.

Finally, we evaluate the integral and get

∫−103xe−2xdx=−3xe−2x2|−10+32∫−10e−2xdx=−3xe−2x2|−10−34e−2x|−10=−32[0e−2(0)−(−1)e−2(−1)]−34[e−2(0)−e−2(−1)]=−32[0+e2]−34[1−e2]=−32e2−34+34e2=−34e2−34=−34(e2+1).

content.knowledge_point: Computing a Definite Integral Using Integration by Parts
content.worked_solution:
Let's use integration by parts. We set

$$
\begin{aligned}u=3x & ⇒ & {u}^{′}=3 \\ {v}^{′}={e}^{-2x} & ⇒ & v=-\frac{{e}^{-2x}}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting the above into the integration by parts formula, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\int u{v}^{′}\,\text{d}x & =uv-\int v{u}^{′}\,\text{d}x \\ \int 3x\cdot {e}^{-2x}\,\text{d}x & =3x\cdot (-\frac{{e}^{-2x}}{2})-\int (-\frac{{e}^{-2x}}{2})\cdot 3\,\text{d}x \\  & =-\frac{3x{e}^{-2x}}{2}+\frac{3}{2}\int {e}^{-2x}\,\text{d}x.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we evaluate the integral and get

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{-1}^{0}3x{e}^{-2x}\,\text{d}x & =-\frac{3x{e}^{-2x}}{2}{|}_{-1}^{0}+\frac{3}{2}{\int }_{-1}^{0}{e}^{-2x}\,\text{d}x \\  & =-\frac{3x{e}^{-2x}}{2}{|}_{-1}^{0}-\frac{3}{4}{e}^{-2x}{|}_{-1}^{0} \\  & =-\frac{3}{2}[0{e}^{-2(0)}-(-1){e}^{-2(-1)}]-\frac{3}{4}[{e}^{-2(0)}-{e}^{-2(-1)}] \\  & =-\frac{3}{2}[0+{e}^{2}]-\frac{3}{4}[1-{e}^{2}] \\  & =-\frac{3}{2}{e}^{2}-\frac{3}{4}+\frac{3}{4}{e}^{2} \\  & =-\frac{3}{4}{e}^{2}-\frac{3}{4} \\  & =-\frac{3}{4}({e}^{2}+1).\end{aligned}
$$

after.name: Question 12
after.worked_solution:
Let's use integration by parts. We set

$$
\begin{aligned}u=x & ⇒ & {u}^{′}=1 \\ {v}^{′}=\operatorname{cos}⁡(2x) & ⇒ & v=\frac{\operatorname{sin}⁡(2x)}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting the above into the integration by parts formula, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\int u{v}^{′}\,\text{d}x & =uv-\int v{u}^{′}\,\text{d}x \\ \int x\cdot \operatorname{cos}⁡(2x)\,\text{d}x & =x\cdot \frac{\operatorname{sin}⁡(2x)}{2}-\int (\frac{\operatorname{sin}⁡(2x)}{2})\cdot 1\,\text{d}x.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we evaluate the integral and get

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{-\pi /4}^{\pi /4}x\operatorname{cos}⁡(2x)\,\text{d}x & ={\frac{x\operatorname{sin}⁡(2x)}{2}|}_{-\pi /4}^{\pi /4}-{\int }_{-\pi /4}^{\pi /4}\frac{\operatorname{sin}⁡(2x)}{2}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\frac{1}{2}x\operatorname{sin}⁡(2x)|}_{-\pi /4}^{\pi /4}+\frac{1}{4}\operatorname{cos}⁡(2x){|}_{-\pi /4}^{\pi /4} \\  & =\frac{1}{2}[\frac{\pi }{4}\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{\pi }{2})+\frac{\pi }{4}\operatorname{sin}⁡(-\frac{\pi }{2})]+\frac{1}{4}[\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{\pi }{2})-\operatorname{cos}⁡(-\frac{\pi }{2})] \\  & =\frac{1}{2}[\frac{\pi }{4}-\frac{\pi }{4}]+\frac{1}{4}[0-0] \\  & =\frac{1}{2}[0]+0 \\  & =0.\end{aligned}
$$

content.knowledge_point: Computing a Definite Integral Using Integration by Parts
content.worked_solution:
Let's use integration by parts. We set

$$
\begin{aligned}u=x & ⇒ & {u}^{′}=1 \\ {v}^{′}=\operatorname{cos}⁡(2x) & ⇒ & v=\frac{\operatorname{sin}⁡(2x)}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting the above into the integration by parts formula, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\int u{v}^{′}\,\text{d}x & =uv-\int v{u}^{′}\,\text{d}x \\ \int x\cdot \operatorname{cos}⁡(2x)\,\text{d}x & =x\cdot \frac{\operatorname{sin}⁡(2x)}{2}-\int (\frac{\operatorname{sin}⁡(2x)}{2})\cdot 1\,\text{d}x.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we evaluate the integral and get

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{-\pi /4}^{\pi /4}x\operatorname{cos}⁡(2x)\,\text{d}x & ={\frac{x\operatorname{sin}⁡(2x)}{2}|}_{-\pi /4}^{\pi /4}-{\int }_{-\pi /4}^{\pi /4}\frac{\operatorname{sin}⁡(2x)}{2}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\frac{1}{2}x\operatorname{sin}⁡(2x)|}_{-\pi /4}^{\pi /4}+\frac{1}{4}\operatorname{cos}⁡(2x){|}_{-\pi /4}^{\pi /4} \\  & =\frac{1}{2}[\frac{\pi }{4}\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{\pi }{2})+\frac{\pi }{4}\operatorname{sin}⁡(-\frac{\pi }{2})]+\frac{1}{4}[\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{\pi }{2})-\operatorname{cos}⁡(-\frac{\pi }{2})] \\  & =\frac{1}{2}[\frac{\pi }{4}-\frac{\pi }{4}]+\frac{1}{4}[0-0] \\  & =\frac{1}{2}[0]+0 \\  & =0.\end{aligned}
$$

after.worked_solution:
Let's use integration by parts. We set

$$
\begin{aligned}u=9x & ⇒ & {u}^{′}=9 \\ {v}^{′}=\operatorname{cos}⁡(3x) & ⇒ & v=\frac{1}{3}\operatorname{sin}⁡(3x).\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting the above into the integration by parts formula, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\int u{v}^{′}\,\text{d}x & =uv-\int v{u}^{′}\,\text{d}x \\ \int 9x\cdot \operatorname{cos}⁡(3x)\,\text{d}x & =9x\cdot \frac{1}{3}\operatorname{sin}⁡(3x)-\int \frac{1}{3}\operatorname{sin}⁡(3x)\cdot 9\,\text{d}x.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we evaluate the integral and get

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{\pi /3}9x\operatorname{cos}⁡(3x)\,\text{d}x & =3x\operatorname{sin}⁡(3x)\,{|}_{0}^{\pi /3}-3{\int }_{0}^{\pi /3}\operatorname{sin}⁡(3x)\,\text{d}x \\  & =3x\operatorname{sin}⁡(3x)\,{|}_{0}^{\pi /3}+\operatorname{cos}⁡(3x)\,{|}_{0}^{\pi /3} \\  & =3(\frac{\pi }{3}\cdot \operatorname{sin}⁡(\pi )-0\cdot \operatorname{sin}⁡(0))+(\operatorname{cos}⁡(\pi )-\operatorname{cos}⁡(0)) \\  & =3(\frac{\pi }{3}\cdot 0-0\cdot 0)+(-1-1) \\  & =-2.\end{aligned}
$$

after.worked_solution:
Let's use integration by parts. We set

$$
\begin{aligned}u=x & ⇒ & {u}^{′}=1 \\ {v}^{′}={e}^{-x} & ⇒ & v=-{e}^{-x}.\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting the above into the integration by parts formula, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\int u{v}^{′}\,\text{d}x & =uv-\int v{u}^{′}\,\text{d}x \\ \int x\cdot {e}^{-x}\,\text{d}x & =x\cdot (-{e}^{-x})-\int (-{e}^{-x})\cdot 1\,\text{d}x.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we evaluate the integral and get

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{-2}^{0}x{e}^{-x}\,\text{d}x & =-x{e}^{-x}{|}_{-2}^{0}+{\int }_{-2}^{0}{e}^{-x}\,\text{d}x \\  & =-x{e}^{-x}{|}_{-2}^{0}-{e}^{-x}{|}_{-2}^{0} \\  & =[-0{e}^{-0}-2{e}^{2}]-[{e}^{0}-{e}^{2}] \\  & =-2{e}^{2}-1+{e}^{2} \\  & =-1-{e}^{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Question 14
?

Evaluate ∫−20xe−xdx.

a
−2−e2
b
1−3e2
c
1+e2
d
−1+e2
e
−1−e2
Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

Let's use integration by parts. We set

u=x⇒u′=1v′=e−x⇒v=−e−x. Substituting the above into the integration by parts formula, we get

∫uv′dx=uv−∫vu′dx∫x⋅e−xdx=x⋅(−e−x)−∫(−e−x)⋅1dx.

Finally, we evaluate the integral and get

∫−20xe−xdx=−xe−x|−20+∫−20e−xdx=−xe−x|−20−e−x|−20=[−0e−0−2e2]−[e0−e2]=−2e2−1+e2=−1−e2.

verification.explanation: The worked solution confirms option e. The antiderivative is −(x+1)e^{-x}; evaluating at 0 and −2 gives −1−e².

content.knowledge_point: Computing a Definite Integral Using Integration by Parts
content.worked_solution:
Let's use integration by parts. We set

$$
\begin{aligned}u=x & ⇒ & {u}^{′}=1 \\ {v}^{′}={e}^{-x} & ⇒ & v=-{e}^{-x}.\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting the above into the integration by parts formula, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\int u{v}^{′}\,\text{d}x & =uv-\int v{u}^{′}\,\text{d}x \\ \int x\cdot {e}^{-x}\,\text{d}x & =x\cdot (-{e}^{-x})-\int (-{e}^{-x})\cdot 1\,\text{d}x.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we evaluate the integral and get

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{-2}^{0}x{e}^{-x}\,\text{d}x & =-x{e}^{-x}{|}_{-2}^{0}+{\int }_{-2}^{0}{e}^{-x}\,\text{d}x \\  & =-x{e}^{-x}{|}_{-2}^{0}-{e}^{-x}{|}_{-2}^{0} \\  & =[-0{e}^{-0}-2{e}^{2}]-[{e}^{0}-{e}^{2}] \\  & =-2{e}^{2}-1+{e}^{2} \\  & =-1-{e}^{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

after.name: Question 15
after.worked_solution:
Let's use integration by parts. We set

$$
\begin{aligned}u=2x\, & ⟹\,{u}^{′}=2 \\ {v}^{′}=\operatorname{sin}⁡(3x) & ⟹\,v=-\frac{1}{3}\operatorname{cos}⁡(3x).\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting the above into  the integration by parts formula, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\int u{v}^{′}\,\text{d}x & =uv-\int v{u}^{′}\,\text{d}x \\ \int 2x\cdot \operatorname{sin}⁡(3x)\,\text{d}x & =-2x\cdot \frac{1}{3}\operatorname{cos}⁡(3x)-\int (-\frac{1}{3}\operatorname{cos}⁡(3x))\cdot 2\,\text{d}x.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we evaluate the integral and get

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{\pi /6}2x\operatorname{sin}⁡(3x)\,\text{d}x & ={-\frac{2x\operatorname{cos}⁡(3x)}{3}|}_{0}^{\pi /6}+\frac{2}{3}{\int }_{0}^{\pi /6}\operatorname{cos}⁡(3x)\,\text{d}x \\  & ={-\frac{2x\operatorname{cos}⁡(3x)}{3}|}_{0}^{\pi /6}+{\frac{2}{9}\operatorname{sin}⁡(3x)|}_{0}^{\pi /6} \\  & =-\frac{2}{3}[\frac{\pi }{6}\operatorname{cos}⁡(3\cdot \frac{\pi }{6})-0\cdot \operatorname{cos}⁡(3\cdot 0)] \\  & +\frac{2}{9}[\operatorname{sin}⁡(3\cdot \frac{\pi }{6})-\operatorname{sin}⁡(3\cdot 0)] \\  & =-\frac{2}{3}[0-0]+\frac{2}{9}[\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{\pi }{2})-\operatorname{sin}⁡(0)] \\  & =\frac{2}{9}.\end{aligned}
$$

\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{\pi /6}2x\operatorname{sin}⁡(3x)\,\text{d}x & ={-\frac{2x\operatorname{cos}⁡(3x)}{3}|}_{0}^{\pi /6}+\frac{2}{3}{\int }_{0}^{\pi /6}\operatorname{cos}⁡(3x)\,\text{d}x \\  & ={-\frac{2x\operatorname{cos}⁡(3x)}{3}|}_{0}^{\pi /6}+{\frac{2}{9}\operatorname{sin}⁡(3x)|}_{0}^{\pi /6} \\  & =-\frac{2}{3}[\frac{\pi }{6}\operatorname{cos}⁡(3\cdot \frac{\pi }{6})-0\cdot \operatorname{cos}⁡(3\cdot 0)] \\  & +\frac{2}{9}[\operatorname{sin}⁡(3\cdot \frac{\pi }{6})-\operatorname{sin}⁡(3\cdot 0)] \\  & =-\frac{2}{3}[0-0]+\frac{2}{9}[\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{\pi }{2})-\operatorname{sin}⁡(0)] \\  & =\frac{2}{9}.\end{aligned}
$$
